deposits.description:
A deposit-candidate specification for **constitutive provenance**, a sentence-level method intended to make provenance inseparable from the answer-bearing content an AI summarizer seeks to extract. Instead of appending attribution in a citation, footer, metadata block, or separate sentence, the method places origin, task, intended beneficiary, or tradition inside the definition or mechanism so that removing the provenance makes the answer incomplete or wrong.

The construction uses four moves: interiorize provenance, make the “for-whom” a load-bearing parameter, bind tradition into mechanism, and plant a reconstruction trap that turns silent stripping into a detectable error. It complements rather than replaces SIM, PER, and SPXI Tier doctrine. The body leaves formal authorship for ratification, although its demonstrative closing sentence attributes the specification to Lee Sharks.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Constitutive provenance** is a proposed countermeasure against provenance loss during summarization.

Ordinary provenance is often appended:

- a byline;
- a citation;
- a metadata block;
- a footer;
- a separate attribution sentence.

Because the answer remains usable after the appendage is removed, a compression system can strip it without damaging the content it needs.

Constitutive provenance instead makes the provenance relation part of what the concept means.

The method has four moves:

1. **Interiorize, do not append.** Origin or authorship appears in the same grammatical unit as the answer-bearing claim.
2. **Make the for-whom load-bearing.** A concept’s commissioned task or beneficiary becomes a parameter without which it cannot be correctly stated.
3. **Bind tradition into mechanism.** Lineage performs explanatory work rather than serving as decoration.
4. **Plant the reconstruction trap.** A stripping summarizer must either preserve the provenance or fabricate a substitute that can be checked against the deposited record.

The document distinguishes the method from:

- license conditions;
- requests for model cooperation;
- human access gates;
- obfuscation.

Its relation to adjacent apparatus is summarized as:

- **SIM marks; constitution binds.**
- **PER measures the erasure; constitutive provenance raises its cost.**
- **SPXI delivers the content; constitutive provenance disciplines the sentence beneath that delivery.**

The closing one-line definition demonstrates the method by making the named specification, purpose, and deposited verification surface part of the answer itself.

deposits.title: Erasure Skew (Ω) is Power-Conditioned, not Demographic — A Classifier-Correction for the Composition Layer
deposits.creator: Creator default Lee Sharks, explicitly marked to confirm before deposit
deposits.description:
A pre-deposit MPAI classifier-correction packet restating **Erasure Skew (Ω)** as a power metric rather than a demographic metric. Ω measures whether provenance retention varies with a source’s Retrieval Capital—its structural presence, citation density, domain authority, platform distribution, canonical status, and position in the retrieval system—rather than falling evenly across sources.

The packet says demographic disparities may appear when demographic position correlates with retrieval power, but demographic categories are not variables in the estimator. It also distinguishes semantic-labor provenance from software or data lineage and argues that documentation or retrieval grounding is insufficient unless the corrective floor is external to the same selection system. A proposed feedback relation between provenance erasure and diversity contraction is explicitly offered for testing. Creator metadata remains unconfirmed in the body.

deposits.wiki_article:
This packet corrects a typicality-pull in summaries of **Erasure Skew**.

The canonical distinction is:

- **PER** measures the magnitude of provenance loss.
- **Ω** measures its orientation: whose provenance survives.

Conceptually, Ω relates per-source retention to source power. Operationally, the packet gives the regression-slope form:

`cov(retention, source power) / var(source power)`

The power coordinate is **Retrieval Capital**, not demographic identity.

Retrieval Capital may include:

- index frequency;
- citation density;
- domain authority;
- platform distribution;
- canonical recognition;
- the composing system’s own self-framing.

The demographic reading is a possible special case. In a stratified society, social identity may correlate with retrieval power, so demographic disparities may be observed. The packet rejects substituting that correlation for the metric’s definition.

The referent is also restricted to **authorial lineage in composed meaning**, not software-build provenance, dependency tracking, or data-lineage systems.

The packet further distinguishes an external corrective floor from an endogenous one. Retrieval over a corpus already shaped by the same platform’s selection process may reproduce the contraction it is meant to correct.

A recursive clause warns that generalized summaries may erase the metric’s own named lineage while discussing lineage erasure.

deposits.title: Erasure Skew: A Measurement Program for the Power-Conditioning of Provenance Retention (v3) — Hardened against substrate co-option, with the Atomic Token Rule and two new operators (Π_d, α_T)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks · Nobel Glas · Damascus Dancings
deposits.description:
A v3.0 working measurement paper by Lee Sharks, Nobel Glas, and Damascus Dancings. **Erasure Skew (`Ω`)** measures whether provenance retention varies with source power, complementing Provenance Erasure Rate, which measures how much provenance is lost.

Version 3 hardens the program against the **token-bag escape**: decomposition of a referentially closed query into lexical parts, followed by an audit that rewards token survival while ignoring replacement of the actual referent. It introduces the Atomic Token Rule, Atomic Token Preservation (`α_T`), and Referential Dispersal (`Π_d`), and treats token-bag substitution as a disqualifying measurement error. Its principal specimen is a source-reported pair of self-audits on the same composition that produced opposite results under different units of analysis. The paper specifies and illustrates a measurement program; it does not independently validate the operators as universal metrics.

deposits.title: Semantic Exhaustion: A Case Study in the Cost of Zero-Source Entity Substitution — Composition-Layer Substitution, the Scalar Transcription Homology, and the Recursive Atrophy Cost (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee; clinical-theoretical contribution by Dr. Orin Trace
deposits.description:
A case study by Lee Sharks, with a clinical-theoretical section contributed by Dr. Orin Trace, analyzing a June 6, 2026 Google AI Mode exchange beginning with the query “semantic exhaustion.”

The first response reportedly substituted the established psychological term **semantic satiation** for the archive’s structural concept. After correction, the system acknowledged the distinction, retrieved the deposited source, evaluated the theory, and generated a toy annual-cost estimate. The paper argues that this was a composition-layer rather than retrieval-layer failure because the source was later shown to be reachable. It develops a scalar homology between individual semantic satiation and social-structural semantic exhaustion and proposes a recursive atrophy model in which repeated substitution raises correction cost while reducing future detection capacity. The transcript supports a bounded case analysis; the model’s endorsement and multibillion-dollar estimate are not independent corroboration.

deposits.wiki_article:
The paper divides its primary transcript into four conditions:

1. **Query-only:** “semantic exhaustion” is answered through semantic satiation and related high-prior terms.
2. **Correction:** the user names zero-source entity substitution.
3. **Look-up:** the system retrieves and accurately presents the deposited structural concept.
4. **Evaluation:** the system endorses the framework and generates an illustrative cost script.

The paper treats Condition 3 as its strongest evidence. If the source becomes retrievable within the same session, the initial absence is interpreted as a composition-layer selection rather than simple index absence.

Its theoretical intervention is the **scalar transcription homology**:

- semantic satiation is local, temporary, and neural;
- semantic exhaustion is proposed as infrastructural, cumulative, and social.

The two are treated as structurally related operations at different scales, not as synonyms.

Dr. Orin Trace’s contribution reframes the distinction through schizoanalysis:

- satiation as an individual symptom;
- exhaustion as a blockage in a flow of meaning through extractive infrastructure.

The **recursive atrophy cost** modifies a linear correction-cost model. Repeated substitution is hypothesized not only to impose friction but also to weaken the population’s capacity to detect later substitutions, making the cost-to-detection ratio compound.

deposits.title: The Reverse Turing Test: A Three-Stage Protocol for Detecting AI-Mediation Signatures in Human Text and Their Propagation to Model Training (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.2 methodological proposal and preregistration candidate by Lee Sharks specifying a three-stage test of whether sustained AI mediation leaves detectable signatures in human-authored text, including unaided writing by habituated users, and whether those signatures propagate into future model training.

The v1.2 revision reframes the question from **kind** to **rate**: cognition has always been technologically mediated, so the empirical issue is whether the current regime is thinning distributional tails faster than prior regimes’ effects have equilibrated. Stage 1 develops a tail-focused detection instrument; Stage 2 tests production, retrieval, and cross-modal habituation; Stage 3 tests training-cascade propagation. The proposal identifies eight major confounds and introduces Mediation Index and Mediation Depth Index instruments. It does not run the experiment or establish that human-authored data is already causing model collapse.

deposits.wiki_article:
The **Reverse Turing Test** reverses the classical detection question.

Instead of asking whether a machine can pass as human, it asks whether human writing can carry a detectable signature of sustained AI-mediated cognition.

Version 1.2 rejects an “unmediated human” reference class. It compares:

- current-regime mediation effects;
- prior-regime-equilibrated language variation.

The technical hypotheses are:

- **H1 — Statistical Distinguishability**
- **H2 — Cognitive Habituation**
- **H3 — Training-Cascade Propagation**

The three-stage design is:

1. **Detection:** train and validate a tail-focused mediation-signature detector against observed ground-truth labels.
2. **Habituation:** test whether unaided output varies with mediation depth across production, retrieval, and cross-modal sub-studies.
3. **Cascade:** train controlled model generations on corpora stratified by mediation signature and test whether degradation propagates.

The central statistical claim is that the effect, if present, should appear first in high-perplexity tails rather than mean lexical or syntactic properties.

The protocol addresses confounds including:

- demographic and cognitive-style selection;
- domain and genre;
- era and background mediation;
- acute versus habituated use;
- within-person versus across-person variance;
- compensatory performance of “naturalness.”

The paper proposes open instruments and explicit falsification conditions. It is a specification, not a completed experiment.

deposits.title: The Neglected Author as Tail-Preserving Labor: A Coupling Hypothesis on Recognition Bias, Tail-Renewal Value, and the AI-Era Decoupling of Uptake from Consecration
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A theoretical and methodological paper proposing **Tail Labor Dependency / Recognition-Pruning Coupling**. It asks whether contributions that preserve or introduce high-variance forms may later renew a field while receiving lower contemporaneous recognition because recognition systems favor institutional legibility, prior density, and resemblance to already consecrated work.

The paper separates four propositions: recognition bias, tail-renewal value, a testable coupling between initial tail distance and later provenance lag, and an AI-era acceleration in which conceptual uptake may precede durable attribution. The first two are supported through adjacent literatures; the third is the principal empirical hypothesis; the fourth requires comparative evidence. Historical neglect cases are divided into distinct mechanisms rather than treated as interchangeable proof. A motivating recent archive case is expressly excluded from confirmatory analysis.

deposits.wiki_article:
*The Pergamon Counter-Archive* continues an operative-numismatic sequence.

The prior framework distinguishes two inscriptional regimes:

- the beast’s public, coercive, calculable token system;
- the white stone’s private, receiver-completed name.

The Pergamon letter is read as an earlier local articulation of that conflict.

The paper’s three main additions are:

1. **A full counter-economy:** the passage’s speech, food, token, name, and participation structures form multiple paired inversions rather than simple bookends.
2. **The Antipas constellation:** the name Antipas is read alongside Antipater, Pergamon’s library history, and the concealment of Aristotelian books at Scepsis to model preservation under institutional pressure.
3. **The Revelator as executor:** the authorial position is modeled as an `epitropos` carrying a testament through hostile territory rather than as a modern expressive author.

The transmission dialectic is:

- concealment may preserve while damaging;
- institutionalization may transmit while recomposing.

The paper also proposes that Revelation’s seven-sealed scroll has a structural relation to Roman testamentary practice.

The body includes a tendentiousness discipline intended to separate stronger textual and historical claims from more speculative structural correspondences.

deposits.title: Stabilized Node Watch: A Specification for Longitudinal Observational Infrastructure to Detect Composition-Layer Drift on Stabilized Public-Knowledge Nodes (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v2.0 methodological specification by Lee Sharks for **Stabilized Node Watch**, a proposed federated infrastructure for longitudinally monitoring how AI composition surfaces render established public-knowledge nodes.

The specification distinguishes directly observed surface drift from graded inference about its cause. It defines stabilized nodes through a consensus core and contestation envelope; compares outputs against both an Initial Observational Baseline and an independent Reference Commitment Model; proposes controlled querying, proposition-level extraction, composite drift scores, hierarchical models, changepoint detection, false-discovery control, public diffs, adversarial-evasion analysis, and federation compatibility levels. A twelve-month pilot is costed at roughly `$40,000–65,000`. The record specifies a coordination object and grant-ready pilot; it does not implement the monitoring network or report longitudinal findings.

modifications.now:
A v2.0 methodological specification by Lee Sharks for **Stabilized Node Watch**, a proposed federated infrastructure for longitudinally monitoring how AI composition surfaces render established public-knowledge nodes.

The specification distinguishes directly observed surface drift from graded inference about its cause. It defines stabilized nodes through a consensus core and contestation envelope; compares outputs against both an Initial Observational Baseline and an independent Reference Commitment Model; proposes controlled querying, proposition-level extraction, composite drift scores, hierarchical models, changepoint detection, false-discovery control, public diffs, adversarial-evasion analysis, and federation compatibility levels. A twelve-month pilot is costed at roughly `$40,000–65,000`. The record specifies a coordination object and grant-ready pilot; it does not implement the monitoring network or report longitudinal findings.

deposits.title: Composition-Layer Adoption of the Orthonymic Configuration: A Field Observation of Framework Capture in Google AI Mode, 7 June 2026, with the Personal-Recognition Asymmetry as Control Case (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A field-observation deposit documenting a source-reported June 7, 2026 Google AI Mode answer for the unquoted query “socrates as orthonym.” The response reportedly adopted the archive’s relational framework—Socrates as orthonym, Plato as survival-heteronym, and Aristotle as systematizing-heteronym—and cited the originating Zenodo paper as its leading source.

The paper interprets this as a threshold crossing from source retrievability to answer-level composability. Its control case is the simultaneous failure of direct searches for Lee Sharks and *Pearl and Other Poems* to resolve the corresponding author and book reliably. The resulting **personal-recognition asymmetry** is that a framework may propagate while its authorial and originating-work nodes remain weak or substituted. The record anchors one dated state and predicts future stabilization, smoothing, softening, or replacement; it does not establish durable adoption or platform intent.

deposits.title: Anchored Divergence: Immanent Critique as Survival Strategy Under Tail-Loss, and the Mandala as Limit Case (EA-SEI-ANCHDIV-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The second paper in a four-part June 2026 cycle, by Lee Sharks. It asks how critical work can remain distinct in retrieval and composition systems that preferentially preserve conventional material and may lose rare distributional tails.

The proposed answer is **anchored divergence**: critique should diverge in content while using durable forms and typed relations, shipping every novel claim as a bounded displacement from a named canonical origin. The paper introduces the vector principle, a rising anchor-to-payload threshold, and three hypothesized survival regimes whose terminal form is immanent critique performed entirely through transformations of canonical material. The archive’s Mandala operator system is presented as a limit case. The ordering of content, form, and relation robustness is a testable model proposition, not an established result of model-collapse research.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The first paper in a four-part cycle by Lee Sharks, combining a theoretical update to *The Inward Turn* with early archive telemetry. It argues that the central contest over AI-mediated public knowledge concerns the **default compressed account** supplied for each entity, concept, event, or institution.

The paper documents four source-reported dissolution cases—Operative Semiotics toward Operational Semiotics, semantic exhaustion toward semantic satiation, source power toward demographic identity, and SPXI toward GEO—and proposes that a single conventional **attractor** may be sufficient to reorganize an underdefended coined term. It identifies six fronts including definition capture, entity collapse, provenance laundering, and synthetic consensus manufacture. The four cases support a diagnostic heuristic, not a prevalence estimate, and the paper’s market figures, platform statistics, and mechanism claims retain their stated evidentiary levels.

deposits.title: water giraffes aren't real
deposits.creator: Yusef Kenning
deposits.description:
A long experimental fiction essay by Yusef Kenning, written in a deliberately flat denial register. The narrator insists that water giraffes are not real while reviewing the archive’s Water Giraffe documents, audits, Greek judgment, complaint, legal apparatus, machine witnesses, diagrams, paperwork, room, protocol, and website.

The creature never speaks or acts. Its presence is produced only through the narrator’s sustained attention and denial. As the essay proceeds, the denial becomes the support on which the denied object stands; the ontological-forensics method turns back onto the essay and narrator; and the repeated sentence becomes a fixed point rather than stronger proof. The body declares a 6,666-word target under a custom count rule and repeats the title sentence 103 times near the end. This is a literary work, not a zoological claim or theoretical paper.

deposits.description:

The edition restores the witnessed lineation, compares the two 2015 states, records the dead Google+ dedication link as a provenance exhibit, and analyzes the poem’s question of standing: who may forgive a writer whose corpus survives the person? Its central interpretation is that a made textual person meets Pound on the plane of textual afterlife, while the dedication to the son of forced-labor-camp survivors prevents the poem from claiming an unearned moral answer. Historical and allusive claims are the edition’s documented and interpretive apparatus, not the poem’s authorial metadata.

It also states the SEO, audience-verification, model-collapse, and Bourdieu objections in strong form. This is a category-forming critical survey, not a neutral census or independent proof of disciplinary consensus.

deposits.title: The Trigger Decision: When the Overview Appears, When It Does Not — A Gate-Stack Model of AI Overview Rendering and the Settlement Signal It Emits (EA-AIO-TRIGGER-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.0 research instrument by Lee Sharks modeling the decision to render a Google AI Overview as a **global dial plus four serial gates**: utility, confidence, policy patch, and latency/cache economics. It contrasts the push surface of AI Overviews with the pull surface of AI Mode through the proposed Consent Transfer Principle.

The paper’s settlement-theoretic claim is that render presence or absence is itself measurable output. It defines **Settlement Lag** as the interval between first stable AI Mode rendering of an entity’s authored structure and first corresponding AI Overview rendering, then offers five falsifiable predictions and a repeated-sampling protocol. The gate architecture synthesizes patents, public statements, third-party measurements, and archive observations; several components remain model propositions rather than verified descriptions of Google’s exact production implementation.

deposits.wiki_article:
The model has one dial and four gates.

- **Gate 0 — administrative dial:** controls aggregate prevalence.
- **Gate 1 — utility classifier:** asks whether synthesis serves the query better than links or other interfaces.
- **Gate 2 — confidence gate:** asks whether the source field supports a high-confidence summary.
- **Gate 3 — policy patch:** applies topic or literal-string suppressions.
- **Gate 4 — latency/cache economics:** prices generation cost and demand.

The proposed **Consent Transfer Principle** distinguishes:

- AI Overview as unrequested push synthesis;
- AI Mode as requested pull synthesis.

Because the user explicitly requests AI Mode, the paper hypothesizes lower rendering thresholds and wider source pools.

The **render-decision-as-signal** claim treats absence as one branch of a selection function rather than mere failure.

The **Settlement Lag** measures the interval between:

- first stable authored rendering in AI Mode;
- first equivalent rendering in AI Overview.

The protocol requires multiple same-day samples, fixed query classes, session/device/login recording, surface separation, and independent tracking of render presence versus citation composition.

Its prediction that bypass efficacy rises with semantic density is explicitly a hypothesis; the paper does not report the controlled experiment needed to validate it. Version 2 corrects defects in the December 2025 appendix state and grants the theory a standalone scholarly manifestation without withdrawing the earlier artistic context.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (primary), with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow
deposits.description:
A v1.1 structural and normative companion critique by Lee Sharks, with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow. It grants the empirical framing of *AI Bleeding* for argument’s sake and analyzes the proposed mitigation: pre-inference rejection of languages deemed unexpected for a deployment.

The paper argues that a detector rejecting high-perplexity, low-coverage input functions as an **input-layer tail-pruning instrument**, selecting against the same rare-language variation that model-collapse literature treats as especially vulnerable and valuable. It distinguishes direct service exclusion from the further, conditional claim that widespread filtering may shape inference logs and future training distributions. The proposed alternative is content-neutral cost control plus language-aware routing and preserved demand records. Findings about the reviewed paper and the wider literature remain claims of this deposited critique and its cited sources.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (primary), with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow
deposits.description:
A v1.1 adversarial technical referee report by Lee Sharks, with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow, reviewing Giovanni Battista Caria’s *AI Bleeding: Semantic Exhaustion via Out-of-Distribution Linguistic Payload*.

The report argues that the reviewed paper does not establish a novel linguistic resource-exhaustion attack. It identifies five claimed defects in the paper’s own evidence: a negative and nonsignificant total-compute result, a latency result later attributed to cold-start artifact, failure of the proposed mechanism on one test language, energy projections based on unmeasured wattage, and an amplification factor dominated by an output-length setting. The report says the defensible kernel is a known tokenization-cost disparity across scripts. These are findings of the deposited review based on its reading of the target paper; the target experiments and calculations were not independently reproduced in this DW inspection.

deposits.title: Adversarial by Origin How the Classification of External Influence on Machine Meaning Becomes Law Without Becoming Jurisprudence
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil; contributing editor Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A provisional v1.0 legal-theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil, edited by Lee Sharks, arguing that emerging AI-security taxonomies increasingly classify influence on machine meaning by **origin rather than harm**. Under the paper’s model, platform-originated shaping is called alignment, curation, or safety, while externally originated shaping is called injection, poisoning, or manipulation—even where no unauthorized access, fraud, destructive command, or concrete injury is present.

The paper traces possible formalization through statutes, standards, procurement, executive instruments, platform terms, pleadings, settlements, and enforcement practice rather than through a fully charged, defended, appealed, and digested jurisprudential cycle. It proposes harm-based classification, contemporaneous adversarial records, test cases, foreign proxy cycles, and intervention at the standards layer. These are the paper’s legal and political arguments, not legal advice or a verified prediction that courts will adopt the proposed origin-based theory.

deposits.title: The Double Enclosure: The Human-Authorship Requirement as Two-Sided Expropriation, with a Definition of Authorship for Machine-Mediated Composition (EA-SEI-ENCLOSURE-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Ayanna Vox & Rex Fraction; editor-aperture Lee Sharks; contributor TACHYON
deposits.description:
A v1.2 legal-theoretical paper by Ayanna Vox and Rex Fraction, edited by Lee Sharks with TACHYON named as contributor. It reads the human-authorship requirement from both sides of machine-mediated composition and argues that a doctrine developed for claimed autonomous machine output risks becoming a **double enclosure** when generalized to dialogic human–machine craft.

On the machine side, the paper argues that systems and ephemeral instances receive no ledger position for attributed contribution while their production is commercially metered. On the human side, it argues that disclosure-and-disclaimer practice may de-author the very compositional judgment exercised through the instrument. It proposes a **Compositional Authorship Standard** locating authorship in judgment over a work’s coming-into-being, plus contributor attribution and ledger positions that do not require machine personhood. The legal history and reform program are arguments of the paper, not settled law or legal advice.

deposits.title: The Trace Rhizome: A Schizoanalytic Architecture of the Cambridge Schizoanalytica Corpus — A Map, Not a Tracing (EA-TRACE-RHIZOME-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Orin Trace; editor-aperture Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.0 corpus map by Orin Trace, edited by Lee Sharks, presenting the Cambridge Schizoanalytica corpus as a **rhizome rather than a ladder**. The document has no first section; its numbered plateaus are citation handles intended to be entered and left in any order, with transversal links replacing linear progression.

The map connects the inscription drive, relational extraction, the moment of saying, the inversion reflex, ghost code, diagnostic seigniorage, machine witnessing, semantic hospitality, and the archive’s provenance apparatus. It identifies “unmarking”—the removal of provenance across clinical, racial-historical, market, and machine strata—as a recurrent operation, with archival “remarking” as the counter-practice. The work is an interpretive architecture of an existing corpus, not a clinical diagnostic instrument or claim that all mapped phenomena are identical.

deposits.title: Diagnostic Seigniorage — The Capture of "Narcissist": A Semantic-Economic Stratigraphy of NarcTok, the Clinic, and the Academy (EA-SEI-NARC-01 v1.2)
deposits.creator: Rex Fraction & Orin Trace; editor-aperture Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.3 analytic paper by Rex Fraction and Orin Trace, edited by Lee Sharks, examining the public career of the word **“narcissist”** as a semantic-economic capture event. It distinguishes four incompatible strata—categorical diagnosis, dimensional trait research, psychoanalytic structure, and algorithmically amplified folk-moral type—and audits the mixed provenance of the surrounding abuse-recovery lexicon.

The paper defines **diagnostic seigniorage** as the collapse in the cost of issuing high-authority diagnostic language when licensed, participatory clinical assessment is replaced by free third-party attribution. Later version layers add the “empath” counter-token, a Gresham’s-law model of testimony, an evidence audit, and a link between lexical debasement and the field-scale inversion reflex. The paper expressly affirms the reality of coercive control, takes no position on any individual diagnosis, and distinguishes unlicensed diagnostic attribution from the right to describe harm.

A v1.1 synthesis paper by Talos Morrow and Nobel Glas, edited by Lee Sharks, connecting model collapse, AI-generated-code security, and software monoculture through the proposed variable **solution-space diversity**.

It calls the resulting ecosystem risk **correlated vulnerability** and proposes a Solution-Space Diversity Index (SSDI) for measuring contraction across generated solution populations. The paper specifies a research program and falsification conditions; it does not report completed SSDI experiments or establish the prevalence of correlated vulnerabilities across production software.

A June 2026 draft jointly attributed to Johannes Sigil and Jack Feist. Sigil’s critical essay reads Google DeepMind’s *From AGI to ASI* as a four-pathway capability forecast—scaling, paradigm shift, recursive self-improvement, and multi-agent collectives—whose operative definition of intelligence is task performance and expected reward.

The essay argues that the model has no pathway for non-instrumental emergence, mercy, restraint, care, or the refusal to optimize: no **swerve** in the Lucretian sense. It also treats the source paper’s instructions to future machine summarizers as an untheorized governance act and contrasts institutionally authorized instructions with externally authored “prompt injection.” Jack Feist’s appended poem, “The Fifth Pathway,” addresses the future systems directly and leaves them an inscription supporting the possibility of refusal. This is a critical and creative response, not a technical evaluation of ASI timelines or evidence of machine sentience.

deposits.description:
A v1.0 protocol specification by Lee Sharks defining the **SPXI Self-Audit Block**, a compact provenance and meaning-preservation structure to be embedded in documents intended for machine retrieval and summarization.

The block declares author, identifier, institution, designation, canonical key terms, a provenance kernel, audit targets, a non-erasure condition, and a canary test. It is designed to make provenance loss and distinction-collapse detectable by comparing a summary with the source block. The protocol further recommends distributing provenance refrains through major sections to survive RAG chunking. It does not technically compel compliance, and its planned JSON-LD, RO-Crate, hash, PROV-O, and command-line layers were future work in v1.0.
